pr_title: Made some slight improvements to the AssetBrowser
pr_body:
This PR adds a few simple improvements to the AssetBrowser. Commit messages should be pretty explanatory. I strongly advise reviewing commit by commit.

P.S.:
Fixes #19187.
pr_comments: Updated as requested.
Question for the audience: why do we even have `AssetBrowser.Supported*Extensions` instead of using what the mod already defines with `SoundFormats`, `SpriteFormats` and `VideoFormats`?  🤔

Clicking on a sound file in the asset browser just directly plays it, could we get Play/Stop buttons instead, like for VQAs?
Playback and extensions as such work fine, though.

> Question for the audience: why do we even have AssetBrowser.Supported*Extensions instead of using what the mod already defines with SoundFormats, SpriteFormats and VideoFormats?

Only a guess, but since multiple extensions can be used for the same format (.tem and .sno for shps etc.), it's probably more efficient to pre-filter by extensions, rather than checking every files' header or something.
On that note, RA and TD asset browsers are missing the .V00-V03 extensions for the voice report variations, as well as the .VAR extension for the alternate music and sound files in original TD mix files.

> Clicking on a sound file in the asset browser just directly plays it, could we get Play/Stop buttons instead, like for VQAs?

The bigger problem (with the same fix) is that the sounds keeps on restarting when you are typing into the search filter.

> Only a guess, but since multiple extensions can be used for the same format (.tem and .sno for shps etc.), it's probably more efficient to pre-filter by extensions, rather than checking every files' header or something.
On that note, RA and TD asset browsers are missing the .V00-V03 extensions for the voice report variations, as well as the .VAR extension for the alternate music and sound files in original TD mix files.

My proposal would be to go from the current (at least in this PR) setup:
```yaml
SoundFormats: Aud, Wav

SpriteFormats: ShpTS, TmpTS, ShpTD

VideoFormats: Vqa

ModelSequenceFormat: VoxelModelSequence

AssetBrowser:
	SpriteExtensions: .shp, .tem, .sno
	ModelExtensions: .vxl
	AudioExtensions: .aud, .wav
	VideoExtensions: .vqa
```

to the `AssetBrowser` node being obsolete by giving each `*Loader` class a list of supported extensions (hardcoded, possibly, but could be made extensible?) and the asset browser querying `SoundFormats`/`SpriteFormats`/etc. directly.
That then got me thinking we can do one better and condense it all into 
```yaml
SupportedFileFormats:
	Sprites: ShpTS, TmpTS, ShpTD
	Models: Vxl # or `Voxel` or `VoxelModelSequence`
	Audio: Aud, Wav
	Video: Vqa
```
to be used by both engine and asset browser alike while maintaining the same functionality that we have with this PR. (ofc the proposal would be left for a separate, possibly follow-up PR).

Disabled auto play of audio files and enabled the Play and Stop buttons.
Doing that exposed issues in both `AudFormat` and `WavFormat`'s `ISoundFormat.LengthInSeconds` implementations (via `AudReader.SoundLength()` and `WavReader.WaveLength()`), so I fixed those as well.
During all this I also noticed an incorrectly installed D2k song and fixed the installers, although that commit (the last one) might want to go to its own PR.

>  During all this I also noticed an incorrectly installed D2k song and fixed the installers, although that commit (the last one) might want to go to its own PR.

Own PR that we can pick to prep, IMO.
Split out the D2k installers fix into #19176 and removed that commit from this branch.

> I can also reliably trigger a crash by selecting an audio file while a sprite animation is playing.

Looks like that is also an issue on `bleed` when you select a voxel while a sprite animation is playing - #19187 😉  That should already be fixed in this PR.
Sounds aren't stopped when you leave the close the asset browser, so if you start playing a song and then cancel you end up with two songs playing at once!

My suggestions:
- Add scrolling to the viewport, when viewing assets larger than the preview space (OpenKrush maps are huge images and way bigger for example)
- When multiple assets have the same filename, selecting one will always display the first one. Entries should point explicit to its package (Several old games have no filenames, so "0.sprite" might be present multiple times)
- Can we add palette support? Basicaly allow the asset browser to load up palettes from assets, and make them selectable without the need to write rules for those. (When implementing a new RE'd game, you might want to avoid writing a huge rules block. Being able to test found palettes might be a nice addition.
- Can we re-layout the asset browser so its inner bounds are tied to its outer bounds? In other words: If we make the outer window 100% width/height, every should properly stretch to the size, instead of sitting in the top left. (did this for OpenKrush, to display larger assets. Palette and close button fit good, everything else is tied to top left.
- Can we add a tooltip to the asset list showing its package? (When having multiple same-named files, you want to see which one it is, and who contains it, avoids the need to manualy cycle through all the packages)

Rebased. Couldn't spot any issues with audio. Added one more commit to add package name to the asset tooltip as @IceReaper requested.
The other requests by @IceReaper are out of scope of what should have been a pretty simple PR. (but the "multiple assets with the same name" issue comes from the fact that for sprites and models we don't load the files, but rather query `SpriteCache`/`ModelCache` by asset name).

I didn't notice any issues with audio; was testing with music playing. The audio side of this is a great help to my scripting work when I'm trying to find the right sound!

The icon .shp's don't have a slider, but are scaled accordingly when you use the slider on something else and then go back. I don't know if you want to lock them at an appropriate size or apply the scaler to them.

TS defender at full scale is quite funny. All the other TS browser issues I saw are present in bleed.

Fixed the braces.
Icons don't get a scale slider because that's inside the container holding the other sprite controls and that is designed to hide when the current sprite only has one frame. There is no trivial way around that so I'd rather skip fixing this at this time.

Fixed the raised style issues.
Investigating the audio stream disposal revealed a few other possible things to change to fix bugs or just add general polish.
Changes were mostly in commits `Fixed AudFormat and WavFormat implementations of ISoundFormat.LengthInSeconds` and `Added manual playing and stopping of audio in the AssetBrowserLogic`.
I suppose this may get asked, so I'd rather have it sooner rather than later: is @Mailaender's +1 still valid, because there were a few more fixes since then?

Rebased.
That means you can now test from the comfort of your .NET 6 environments 😎 
Also ran into trouble with the changes from #19681 so will need help with the TD asset browser. @dragunoff 
Fixed a bunch more things, including a couple of issues in OggLoader and Mp3Loader. The notable new changes are in new commits, while several not mention-worthy changes have been fixed in the original commits.

Sadly this has turned from "simple AssetBrowser improvements" to mostly an audio parser refactor, but I hope we're finally good to go.
Updated the scale sliders position. Also added hiding of the palette controls.
Thanks. Especially, the mixing of different sound formats without a crash is a huge benefit to modders.

[ModSDK Changes](https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRAModSDK/wiki/Update-notes:-Release-20210321-to-next-release/_compare/bc363c71915a9ccbd0a437698163b6b56ce5996f...62efe6ade0241dc12786406f8fd8f47d63148caf)

review_comments: Presumably we need to dispose any existing instance assigned to `currentAudioStream ` before reassigning?

That is already handled by `LoadAsset` (the current method) calling `ClearLoadedAssets` as the first thing it does. (Please correct me if I'm wrong ... after 1625372516 rebases and fixes there's a non-zero possibility I may have messed something up again)
Brought it back in one of the new commits.
